beginner.headline: US Government Lawyer Avoids Questions About Nvidia
beginner.brief: Todd Blanche, a top US government lawyer, did not answer some questions about Nvidia. He did not say whether the government was checking the company. Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia's leader. Trump said he helped Huang get his job back. Some US lawmakers, who make laws, want answers about Trump's part in Huang's return. Huang is still expected to answer lawmakers' questions next week. Huang said sorry to Nvidia workers on Tuesday, according to reports. He said his mistakes were very bad.

intermediate.headline: US Attorney General Avoids Questions About Nvidia Investigation
intermediate.brief: US Attorney General Todd Blanche praised Nvidia but refused to say whether the company was under federal investigation. Huang was reinstated less than two weeks after being forced to resign. Huang is due to appear before Congress next week to answer questions about national security concerns. These concerns involve his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy who led Megaspeed, a customer of Nvidia based in Singapore. The US commerce department said it was preparing to blacklist Megaspeed, meaning it planned to place the company under official restrictions. The commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 over possible violations of rules limiting chip exports. Nvidia's board said it was confident that giving Huang his position back posed no national security risk. Trump said he had spoken to Nvidia's directors and convinced them to bring Huang back. The board said its decision served the best interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Nvidia's share price rose more than 31% on Monday after the news that Huang would lead the company again. The share price closed down nearly 6%, although it remained above its level at the end of the previous week. Huang reportedly apologised to Nvidia employees on Tuesday and said he had made serious mistakes.

advanced.headline: US Attorney General Sidesteps Questions About Possible Nvidia Investigation
advanced.brief: While describing Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen”, US Attorney General Todd Blanche declined to clarify whether the chipmaker was under federal investigation. Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated chief executive Jensen Huang’s security clearance. Huang regained his position less than two weeks after being forced to resign following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang is due to face congressional scrutiny next week over national security concerns about his relationship with an alleged Chinese spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. The commerce department announced that it was preparing to blacklist Megaspeed, which was suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China. In a joint statement, the commerce and justice departments said they had begun investigating Megaspeed in 2024 over potential breaches of export controls, rules governing which goods may be sent abroad. Blanche emphasised that the justice department had hundreds of export investigations under way at any given time. Nvidia’s board defended its abrupt reversal on Huang’s leadership as serving the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. The board said it had received input from senior government officials and was confident that Huang’s reappointment posed no national security risk. Trump said he had spoken to Nvidia’s directors and persuaded them to bring Huang back. Senator Pete Ricketts argued that Huang’s conduct did not absolve Nvidia of its responsibility to answer concerns about national security and unaccounted-for chips. Congressman Robert Garcia said Trump’s direct involvement in the decision raised serious questions about national security and corruption. Senator Ruben Gallego called for an investigation into stock positions held before the reappointment announcement. Although Nvidia shares closed nearly 6% lower, they remained above their level at the end of the previous week. Monday’s increase had exceeded 31% following news of Huang’s return. Trump said he would consider pardoning Huang for any potential criminal activity, while indicating that he did not expect a pardon to be needed.
